A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Auto Cherry-Picker (ACP). Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations, downstream detection, segmentation and VQA results, and ablations, including the appendix experiment comparing scene-graph generators.

after.justification: v2 retains original ACP experiments and adds selection comparisons, data-scaling results, layout-generator ablations, and layout-metric evaluations.

M1.justification: The overall LLM, diffusion-model and image-filter pipeline is retained. However, CLIS-L changes from a weighted sum of separately maximized component similarities in v1 Eqs. 4–9 to a percentile of combined per-reference similarities in v2 Eq. 4. This changes selection within the existing layout filter. Sampling object lists from training annotations was already described in v1 Section 3.3.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation using HRS spatial-composition cases in Appendix 10.2 and Figure 13. The principal COCO, LVIS, MME and GQA datasets and downstream task coverage remain. Moving the CLIS-I ablation from COCO to LVIS does not introduce a new downstream domain.

E2.justification: The principal generation and downstream baseline sets remain, but v2 substantially expands comparisons testing the proposed components. It adds a random-selection control alongside CLIP and CLIS, a CLIP-text filtering variant, ACP using ground-truth layouts, average aggregation as a CLIS-L control, and qualitative comparison with HRS. These appear in Figure 1(e), Tables 5, 6 and 8, and Figure 13.

E3.justification: v1's CLIS-L correlation study uses thresholds of 50 and 70 with varying sample counts; v2 uses four score bands with 1.3K samples each. The CLIS-I ablation changes from 1K samples evaluated with Faster R-CNN on COCO to 4K samples with Mask R-CNN on LVIS, selecting one of four images per scene graph. New selection, scaling, layout-generator and layout-swap experiments introduce additional controlled protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds data-volume sensitivity through 100K samples, generated-versus-ground-truth layout ablations, layout-swap and aggregation analyses, score-distribution plots, and HRS case studies. It also revises the CLIS-I component ablation. The appendix LLM-size experiment and original qualitative CLIP/YOLO examples are retained. Table 8's rows and discussion compare average with percentile aggregation, despite its caption referring to Max.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty around performance estimates. v2's new score-distribution plots describe variation among generated samples rather than uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerous results, including rare-category mask AP of 15.3 at 100K samples and 12.2 versus 11.3 for generated versus ground-truth layouts. The 50K result of 14.5 and principal downstream tables remain unchanged. CLIS-L correlation and CLIS-I ablation results are reported under changed conditions, not as same-setting improvements. Table 1 adds CLIP/YOLO values for several generation baselines, while Figure 6 omits several metrics previously reported in v1 Table 2.

T1.justification: CLIS-L receives a non-equivalent mathematical refinement: aggregation changes from separate component maxima followed by weighting to percentile aggregation after combining per-reference scores. v2 Appendix 7.2 also specifies a low-score penalty and Z-score normalization. These changes concern the existing metric's definition; neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds object combinations drawn from real-data priors and alignment with real distributions, qualifying v1's arbitrary-object-list framing. The introduction's headline rare-category mask AP gain increases from 5.2 to 6.0 points, corresponding to the new 100K setting. The central ACP, CLIS and downstream-correlation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for percentile aggregation, tolerance of errors in data priors, and benefits of synthetic layouts through reduced overlap, larger objects and layout-level augmentation. It interprets scaling saturation around 50K samples as an efficiency tradeoff. Limitations are revised toward prior-construction costs, evaluation accuracy and discarded synthetic samples, replacing v1's emphasis on inherited foundation-model limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds image-captioning and text-similarity prompts, SDXL-refinement information, CLIS-L computation details, filtering thresholds and rejection rates, and dataset/split descriptions in Appendices 6–8. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that every disclosed component is newly implemented. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit X-Paste/ACP iteration budgets and COCO prefilter description. Some scoring parameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of SLD, RPG, DALL-E for Detection, HRS, T2I-CompBench and detector-based filtering, while trimming the self-supervised-learning discussion. These changes sharpen comparisons with related generation and evaluation approaches while retaining the overall research positioning. Publication updates and the consolidated LMD reference are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Task Formation becomes a broader Preliminary section, experimental explanations are reorganized, and appendices A–D become a separately organized supplement with Sections 6–10. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, moves and expands Figure 1, redraws the comparison and pipeline diagrams, and converts correlation tables into Figure 6. It adds scaling, layout-comparison and distribution figures, expands Table 1, and splits the former Table 5. Original appendix examples remain as Figures 12, 14 and 15 with presentation changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central filtering and layout-generation contributions. Equal-sized CLIS-L groups address v1's confounding between sample quality and quantity, while random/CLIP selection and ground-truth-layout controls better isolate component benefits. Added prompts and filtering settings improve reproducibility. Unspecified scoring parameters, absent experimental uncertainty and lost X-Paste iteration details remain limitations, but the stronger experimental support provides a substantial net improvement.
